questions.history: A emits "1.0" after subscription and B has "2.0" ready.
questions.prediction: Parent is expected to yield "2.0" under this gate. The merge should yield only "1.0" and complete.
questions.basis: The configured order gives A first refusal. The landed test controls emission without using a timer.
questions.refutation: "2.0" arrives before A’s decision or the subscriber gets two results.

questions.history: Replace A by an immediately empty Mono. B emits "2.0".
questions.prediction: Both versions should produce exactly "2.0" then completion.
questions.basis: Empty means no version was resolved, so B is the first resolver with an answer.
questions.refutation: The result stays empty, fails, or contains any other version.

questions.history: Keep B ready but count subscriptions to it with Mono.defer. After subscription make A fail with a distinct sentinel exception.
questions.prediction: Parent can return "2.0" and cancel A. The merge should propagate the sentinel and leave B’s subscription count at zero.
questions.basis: The earlier resolver can reject an invalid value. Instrumenting B reveals speculative work even if the final error happens to be correct.
questions.refutation: A value masks the error, a different exception escapes, or B’s counter advances on the merge.
